verdict: Mostly trustworthy and close to ready to hand to the team. Every headline count in the front matter and Appendix A matches _context.json and a recount of items.verified.json: 260 baseline capabilities (142/52/22/44) and every per-category figure quoted in 1.2, tiers 24/41/12 before and 24/35/18 after verification, 61 Partial, 3 Stub, 11 Absent, 2 Planned, verdicts 8 keep, 61 reword, 8 demote, 33 efforts revised, 24 reference checks (2 confirmed, 22 corrected in part), 14 wrong prevalence counts, 786 records, 322 clusters, 10 ADR topics. The 1.4 Priority table and all five wave tables show the verified tier, effort, status and wave for all 77 items. The ADR lists in 1.5 and 9.3 match adrNeeded, and every ADR-flagged item sits under a topic. The ten headlines agree with their cards and the code verification, and the 61 common-ground rows and 14 shipped count match _inputs.table-stakes.json. The document answers all six points of the brief: common gaps (section 2), best of breed (3), differentials (7), nice-to-haves separated (section 6, W5), three tiers, and a read-only audit. Fix these before circulation: one strength contradicts a Priority card (Quarry profile routes have no ZDR check, F-t2-020); the exec summary treats the confirmed search-cache cross-tenant hole as an open question; Appendix A's '51 Priority' is not supported by the consolidator data (44 of 121); the prevalence denominator (4 vs 3) is defined inconsistently across the reading guide, section 2, cards and Appendix A; and the generated Appendix B still shows refuted best references for F-t2-001 and F-t2-024. The rest are small wording, tag and cross-reference fixes. Appendix A states REA's limits honestly: heap exhaustion, no string-literal indexing, MSIX loader refusal and timeouts, so most app evidence is SRC; Apify is documentation only; nothing was launched.
